reason: Not functional: a card image linking to the new students guide. The heading and blurb sit outside the link, so "Welcome letters" is the link's only accessible name and it names the picture rather than the destination.

Functional: a safety topic link. The href is /safety/flood, the image file is Flood.png, the visible label beside it reads "Flood", and the alt reads "Wildfire". A person listening is told the wrong hazard and sent to the right page.

Not functional: a portrait in a story card. The alt names the graduate and her award accurately, but the headline is outside the link, so the alt is the link's only name and it does not say where the link goes. Same shape as fi-2087.

Functional: a link to the publication brochures page, labelled "Brochures" in the visible text beside it. The alt says "Cooperative Observers", which is a different NWS programme, so the announced name and the destination do not match.

Not functional: a scenic photograph in a card linking to undergraduate study. The alt describes the view at dusk, which tells a person nothing about the link, and the heading "Undergraduate" is outside the link where it cannot help.

Functional: an icon-only link to the service's Facebook account. The alt names whose account and which service, which is the destination and more than the glyph could carry. Same pattern as fi-10291 and fi-4897.
Not functional: a scenic photograph in a card linking to postgraduate study. Same template and same defect as fi-2240 on the same page.

Functional: the Government of Canada signature links to the site's own root. The alt is the bare government name, with nothing to say the link goes home, and the invisible French span beside it repeats the same name in the other official language.

Not functional: an aerial photograph in a story card. The alt describes the skyline and leaves the acronym GBU unexpanded, so a person hears an initialism and a description of a view instead of where the link goes.

Functional: the App Store badge links to the park service app. The alt transcribes the words on the badge, and those words happen to name both the action and the destination, which is what the criteria ask for.
